answer: Each identity files one karst garden soil sample in an onyx-sealed jar, with a stated carbon figure and a 70 bond. A lab assays the sample under the applicant key; a result over 5 percent from the filed figure, or a reused jar serial, burns the bond. The first assay costs 34, the k-th 34+7(k-1), the 1000th 7027, so a thousand fake filings cost 3,530,500 in assay fees and tie up 70,000 in bonds. A rented-sample ring fails because a rented jar keeps the renter seal and cannot pass under the borrower key. Honest gardeners spend 34 once and recover the bond after one epoch.
